summary:
Martian Story is a browser game that turns scattered NASA Mars data into a world you can walk. You crash-land in Jezero Crater and must survive: salvage the wreck, build a habitat and solar array, and make your own oxygen and water with the help of K-7, a support robot.

The ground under your feet is real. Terrain comes from the USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE elevation model at 1 m per pixel; the landing site reads -2569.92 m against NASA's recorded -2569.91 m. Perseverance drives its actual 45 km route, the sun follows NASA's Mars24 clock, the weather comes from the rover's MEDA station, and CRISM orbital data shows where minerals lie. Gravity is 0.38 g and sound is muffled by the thin CO2 air.

Most people meet Mars only as flat pictures and numbers. Martian Story lets students learn the planet by living on it, and gives future crews a way to know the ground before they land. It runs in any modern browser with nothing to install.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Martian Story is a survival game set in Jezero Crater. The ship Kestrel crashes on approach and the player, with the robot K-7, must stay alive: watch oxygen, power, water and radiation; carry crates and regolith; build a habitat, solar array and grow lights; and finally launch home. A journal tracks missions and unlocks the real science behind each system.

HOW IT WORKS

- Terrain: the USGS Mars 2020 HiRISE DTM (1 m/px) and 25 cm orthomosaic, with the JPL/USGS CTX DEM and MOLA for the horizon. It is drawn with a CDLOD quadtree on WebGL2, with ray-traced soft shadows against the real elevation. Where the stereo data has gaps (9.31% of the main tile), we fill them with coarser CTX elevation and show those areas desaturated, so filled-in ground is never shown as measured (press M).

- Rover: Perseverance drives its real 703 waypoints and 556 drive segments through sol 1980 (45.13 km), from NASA MMGIS.

- Time and sun: the Mars24 algorithm (Allison & McEwen 2000) places the sun at 18.44 N, 77.45 E.

- Weather: Perseverance MEDA pressure, temperature and wind drive the HUD, the survival temperature and the wind sound.

- Minerals: MRO CRISM summary parameters (olivine, carbonate, hydrated minerals). Press K.

- Rover media: press P to see the real Mastcam-Z and Navcam photos taken nearest you, and the RIMFAX radar if the rover sounded that spot.

- Physics: 0.38 g gravity, slope-limited footing, and sound filtered for a 610 Pa CO2 atmosphere. All audio is synthesized in code; there are no sound files.

- Survival numbers (oxygen per person, MOXIE output, solar power, radiation dose) come from NASA ECLSS, radiation and surface-power reports. They are cited in the repo's reports folder.

TOOLS

JavaScript ES modules, WebGL2 and three.js (no bundler, no build step), a small Go static server, and Python scripts to process the NASA/USGS data. It runs in any WebGL2 browser and is hosted on GitHub Pages.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Students and the public explore Mars as a place rather than a picture, on ground that is measured, not invented. Future crews and mission planners could rehearse walking the real terrain before landing.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It is a game, but every layer is honest about where its data comes from. The README has a table of what is real and what is synthesized.

Use of SI: Parts of the code and documentation were written with the help of Claude (Anthropic) through Claude Code; those commits are marked "Co-Authored-By: Claude" in the git history.

Team Butterfly, Cumilla, Bangladesh.
